params.body:
The view count sat among the status chips, first in the row, and it looked misplaced because it was.

Two reasons, and the second one explains the odd spacing.

**It is not a status.** The chips beside it say what the car *is*: sold, draft, on the marketplace, in option, Car-Pass. The count says what other people did. I wrote exactly that in the comment above its CSS and then put it in the most prominent position in that group anyway.

**`.ui-chips` is a two-column grid**, not a flowing row. So the count took a whole grid cell of its own, which pushed "Op Stocklist" to the far side of the cell and shoved Car-Pass onto the next line. The wide gap in the middle was the grid doing what it was told.

## Where it goes instead

Onto the line that already carries the facts about this car, behind year, kilometres and body style:

```
BMW 320d Touring
2020 · 145.000 km · Break · 👁 3
```

That line is where quiet facts about a car belong, it flows as text instead of occupying a grid cell, and the count stops competing with the lifecycle badge. The readout with the split between website and platform still appears on hover.

## Verified

`test_the_count_stands_with_the_car_and_not_among_the_status_chips` asserts the old class is gone and that the count now appears before the status cell in the markup. Putting it back among the chips is the obvious tidy-up for somebody who did not see this, so it is named rather than left to comments.

The class moves from `ui-chip-viewed` to `ui-viewed`, since it is no longer a chip. `StylesheetSyntaxTest` checks that every `ui-` class in a view is defined and every one in the stylesheet is used, so the rename had to happen on both sides at once.

`npm run build` green. Local suite: the same nine failures as on a clean `main` in my environment.
params.title: The view count stands with the car, not among the status chips
